title: Cylindrical base
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and set the translation vector to zero point three seven five, zero, and zero. In the first face, draw the first loop consisting of eight lines. Start from the origin at zero, zero and draw the first line to zero point zero zero two nine, zero. Continue with the second line to zero point zero zero two nine, zero point zero zero three nine, then the third line to zero point zero zero five nine, zero point zero zero three nine. Draw the fourth line to zero point zero zero five nine, zero point zero one five six, and the fifth line to zero point zero zero two nine, zero point zero one five six. Add the sixth line to zero point zero zero two nine, zero point zero one nine five, and the seventh line to zero, zero point zero one nine five. Finally, complete the loop by drawing the eighth line back to the origin. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero one nine five. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translating it using the vector zero point three seven five, zero, and zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch zero point three seven five units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body from this extrusion. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base are length zero point zero zero five eight five nine three seven five, width zero point zero one nine five three one two five, and height zero point three seven five.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0029, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0029, 0.0039) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0039) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0156) \
     .lineTo(0.0029, 0.0156) \
     .lineTo(0.0029, 0.0195) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0195) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.375)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, so we use rotation matrices
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation matrix
# that can be applied as follows:
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90)

# Apply the translation vector
r = r.translate((0.375, 0.0, 0.0))

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0059) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0136) \
     .lineTo(0.0059, 0.0195) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0195) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.1875, both=True)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.375, 0.0, 0.0], so we need to translate the object by this vector
r = r.translate((0.375, 0.0, 0.0))

# Overall: X=0.3750, Y=0.0059, Z=0.0195

total_y = 0.0059

pts = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (total_y, 0.0),
    (total_y, step_h),
    (plate_y, step_h),
    (plate_y, total_z),
    (0.0, total_z),
    (0.0, 0.0),
]

r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .polyline(pts)
    .close()
    .extrude(0.3750)
